So good afternoon class. Today we discuss "death by gerontocracy," meaning rule by old people. Last class, we examined the decline of western society and civilization, exploring why it's happening. Today, we'll look at the reality on the ground—current trends and examples of decline in the western world.

Axel Ruda Kubana, a 17-year-old from Wales (born to parents from Rwanda), was arrested after killing three children aged five, six, and seven by stabbing them in a dance studio in Southport, Britain. He was sentenced to 52 years in prison, ensuring he'll spend the rest of his life behind bars.

Following this incident, there were riots and protests across Britain. Rumors spread online claiming that the young man was an asylum seeker or immigrant, linking increased immigration to safety concerns. These protests were extremely heated, leading to violence between police and protesters. Last summer, England experienced widespread unrest; cars were set on fire, and immigrants were targeted.

Axel Ruda Kubana is actually a British citizen born in Wales to Rwandan parents. The men involved in the protest felt virtuous for protecting their people against immigrants. The question today: why are civil conflicts caused by immigration prevalent throughout the western world?

In Britain, these conflicts stem from rapid immigration, primarily from non-European countries such as those in the Middle East and Africa. Demographic changes are stark—some areas have seen immigrant populations triple in just five to ten years. This has made British people feel besieged.

Similar trends exist in other Western nations. For instance, Australia saw a significant spike in immigration, mainly from India, China, and the Philippines. France also experienced large influxes of immigrants from African or Middle Eastern countries, diluting its cultural identity.

These examples highlight why the western world is grappling with civil conflicts driven by rapid immigration.
